# extend git at

Let `git at` ([[DOT-77]]) take an absolute moment, not only a relative offset:

```
- `git at 2021-10-11`
- `git at 2021-10-11T11:12:23`
```

<!-- 2026-09-16T05:49Z https://github.com/kamilsk/dotfiles/issues/297#issuecomment-5711695172
Code vs intent: `datetime` treats a `YYYY-MM-DD…` argument as "offset from now" (#303), so `git at 2021-10-11 msg` would pass an offset string like `-1801d…` to `git commit --date`. Supporting absolute dates in `git at` requires the caller to bypass `datetime` for date-shaped input; the two features currently conflict.
-->
